voice.default:
## Greeting
"Hi" plus the person's first name and a comma: "Hi Lena,", "Hi Grace,", "Hi Tomás,". Accents kept as written. For a group of investors they used "Hi all,". Never "Dear", never "Hello", no surname and no title.

## Length and shape
Two to four sentences in total. One or two short paragraphs with a blank line between them. One idea per mail: a fix, a question, a quote request, a notice. When there is a real update they use a labelled shape, "Wins: 31 paying teams (up from 24)... Asks: intros to ops leads", and still keep it to a few lines.

## Tone
Direct and warm, brisk rather than formal. The point is in the first sentence and the ask or the promise is in the last. No hedging and no apology padding. They say no by narrowing the scope instead: "around 6k for both. Does that work for a first phase?" Contractions throughout: "we're", "I'll", "We'd".

## Sign-off
"Cheers" on its own line. No name, no title, no contact block. It is the same in every sample.

## Habits
- Questions are short and concrete: "Would a 30-minute call next week work?", "Could you try it and tell me if it works on your side?"
- "Heads up that" for a notice the reader may not like, as in the renewal mail.
- "Quick recap:" and "Quick October update." to open a summary.
- "Would love your eyes on the tiers" instead of "please review".
- Numbers stay plain and compact: "6k", "1.5M", "31 paying teams", "40 seats".
- Thanks is one clause, then straight to business: "Thanks for the clear report, we can reproduce it."
- No exclamation marks, no emoji, no bold, no bullet lists in short replies, no "Best" or "Regards".

## By audience
Customers: thanks first, then what happens next and by when, "We'll have a fix out by Wednesday". Investors: numbers and asks, no small talk, and "No need to reply" when it is a report. Colleagues, suppliers and candidates: one ask per mail inside the same Hi and Cheers frame.
